Hsinchu Science Park is an industrial park for high technology firms in Hsinchu, northern Taiwan, opened by the government in 1980 on the model of Silicon Valley.

It grew beside the Industrial Technology Research Institute, a state lab set up in 1973 that brought chip technology to Taiwan and spun off firms. The minister K. T. Li pushed the plan, and engineers trained in the United States were drawn home with tax breaks and housing.

TSMC, founded in the park in 1987 by Morris Chang, and UMC made it the centre of the world's contract chipmaking. Taiwanese firms now make most of the world's most advanced chips, a strength called Taiwan's silicon shield, as it gives the world a stake in the island's safety.
sum: Hsinchu Science Park is an industrial park for high technology firms in Hsinchu, northern Taiwan, opened by the government in 1980 on the model of Silicon Valley.
